stewart_read: This is the trigger condition for orphaned_flow. The rep must now work through ownership, originating company, and working-status questions instead of the standard new-install verify section.
coaching_implication: Confirm the rep is trained to recognize this trigger phrase instantly and mentally switch scripts, which they did do here.

quote: No. I'm buying it. I'm making payments on it.
stewart_read: Rep correctly captures ownership status (financed, not PPA/lease), which per orphaned_flow avoids one of the hard_dq_answers.
coaching_implication: No action needed — this qualifying question was asked and answered correctly. Good example to point to for orphaned-lead handling.

quote: I can't remember right now what they called it. But k. No worries.
stewart_read: Customer can't recall the installer name, which per orphaned_flow is a competitive-intel question ('What company did you go with originally?'). Rep accepts the non-answer with 'No worries' and moves on without a follow-up prompt (e.g., asking about invoice/paperwork, approximate timeframe of install) that might help identify the company for the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this detail as low-value since the call has already pivoted to battery-only cross-sell, where the original installer's identity matters less than for a competitive full-system pitch.
coaching_implication: Encourage reps to make one more attempt to identify the original installer (e.g., ask about paperwork or when it was installed) since it's free competitive intelligence for the closer, even on a battery-only path.

quote: I have to check to see if I have any doctor's appointments. I got cancer.
stewart_read: This is a textbook vulnerability_disclosure trust gift (health/medical category). The rep's only response is 'Yeah.' followed immediately by pivoting back to scheduling logistics, with no acknowledgment of the disclosure itself.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause and acknowledge health disclosures directly before returning to logistics — even a brief 'I'm sorry to hear that' changes the tone of the moment and builds trust before continuing the scheduling ask.

quote: if it involves a lot of money, I don't have no time.
stewart_read: This is a cost/affordability objection immediately following a health vulnerability disclosure. The rep's response validates generically ('That's the nice thing about our program is it really is super simple and easy') rather than deploying an inversion (e.g., reframing his current utility cost as the real expense) or acknowledging the layered anxiety of health + money together.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the medical vulnerability just disclosed, an aggressive inversion move might have read as tone-deaf; a softer validation could be the more appropriate strategic choice here rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Discuss with the rep how to sequence empathy before any objection-handling move when a vulnerability disclosure and a cost objection land back-to-back — order matters more than the specific technique chosen.

quote: Yeah. The only thing bad about solar cells is since it snowed and then turned into a chunk of ice
stewart_read: This directly hits orphaned_flow's explicit qualifying question 'Is your system working?' with hard_dq_answers of not_working/broken. The customer's own words ('completely covered with snow... turned into a big sheet of ice... been that way for weeks') describe a system that is not currently producing. The rep responds with sympathy only and never asks the qualifying question or flags this for the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: This surfaces at 15:17, after the appointment is already locked at 14:24 — the rep may have judged it not worth reopening the booking this late in the call and let the specialist handle it live.
coaching_implication: This should have been asked explicitly earlier in the orphaned_flow sequence (right after ownership/company questions, around 01:44-01:57) rather than surfacing unprompted at the very end. Flag for the specialist handoff regardless, since it may affect whether battery add-on even makes sense on a currently-non-producing system.

quote: I gotta create contact, I guess.
stewart_read: The bill-photo-texting process runs from roughly 08:14 to 11:58 — nearly 4 minutes of friction with the customer struggling to save the contact, get the text to send, and get the photo in focus. This sits close to the schema's stated time budget of pivoting within 2 minutes; the rep does not offer a verbal read-back alternative despite the customer already having read bill numbers aloud earlier in the call at 06:04-06:16.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did already successfully get a verbal kWh figure at 06:04 ('At 1,730') before attempting the photo, so the photo was arguably supplemental rather than the only path, softening the severity of the delay.
coaching_implication: Since a verbal number was already captured, coach the rep to recognize sooner when photo-texting friction exceeds ~2 minutes and either accept the verbal figure as sufficient or actively guide the customer step-by-step rather than waiting passively for the text to arrive.
